source_documents.title: Polymorph crystal packing effects on charge transfer emission in the solid state

reference_evidence_units.quote: The donor N,N-dimethylaniline and acceptor naphthalimide groups are twisted with respect to each other; the degree of twist is marginally different for the two structures.
reference_evidence_units.subject: DMIM

reference_evidence_units.quote: Very weak room temperature emission was observed for DMIM in a CHCl3 solution, but crystals deposited on a glass slide glowed when irradiated at 488 nm using a fluorescence microscope.
reference_evidence_units.subject: DMIM

reference_evidence_units.quote: One key point to note for DMIM, which is somewhat distinctive to other literature examples, is the observation of photoinduced electron transfer within the dyad in the crystalline state.
reference_evidence_units.subject: DMIM
reference_evidence_units.statement: PET within the dyad in the crystal; emission is charge-recombination fluorescence from the CT state.

reference_evidence_units.quote: The origin of the effect for DMIM appears to be alterations in rate constants for non-radiative decay.
reference_evidence_units.subject: DMIM polymorphs

reference_mechanisms.label: PET_ET
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Photoinduced electron transfer within the twisted dyad gives a CT state whose recombination fluorescence is the solid-state emission.

reference_mechanisms.label: RADIATIVE_RATE_STATE_BALANCE
reference_mechanisms.rationale: The polymorph difference is explained by different non-radiative rate constants.
